blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The NGT has jurisdiction over all civil cases where a substantial question relating to the environment is involved.
NGT handles environmental matters under 7 specific scheduled laws, including the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006 are explicitly excluded from NGT jurisdiction.
The tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908, but is guided by the principles of Natural Justice.
Any appeal against the award, decision, or order of NGT lies directly to the Supreme Court of India within 90 days.
Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006 DO NOT fall under NGT jurisdiction—a very common UPSC elimination option.
NGT is guided by Principles of Natural Justice and NOT bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 or the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
An appeal against any order of NGT can be filed directly in the Supreme Court within 90 days.
